 Welcome to the Beast Mastery Hunter rotation guide for ! This guide will teach you all about the optimal rotation for Beast Mastery Hunter across its various talent builds. It will cover both core ability cadence and cooldown usage in dungeons and raids for .

Beast Mastery Hunter Rotation in 

Beats Mastery Hunter generates most of its resources passively, either through passive focus regeneration or through your abilities coming off cooldown. Your goal is to spend your focus wisely while optimizing the cooldowns of your abilities effectively. The current design of the spec is also heavily based around your main cooldown, so optimizing the amount of powerful abilities in your cooldown window is important. 

 

 

 
 Optimize your cooldown window Make sure your Bestial Wrath is used on cooldown as often as possible and that you take full advantage of all the resources it gives you, such as Stampede! , Wailing Dead and Withering Fire .
 

 

 
 

 
 Maximize your Kill Commands : You want to make sure that Kill Command never reaches two charges, that they're always buffed by Nature's Ally , and that you are able to cast as many of them as possible during your cooldown window.
 

 

 
 

 
 Manage your pets: Make sure your pets are always attacking the correct target and that you are effectively moving them when necessary and swapping when you want them to, ideally using Dash . 
 

 

Beast Mastery Hunter Starter Guide

 Best Beast Mastery Hunter Rotation

The priority for Beast Mastery Hunter is aimed towards keeping powerful spells on cooldown, and filling in the gaps with the less powerful spells. There isn't much in terms of resource management. You work your way down the priority list, and use the more powerful abilities as they become available. Below, we break down the main priority lists for Beast Mastery Hunter: your Single-Target Rotation, your AoE Rotation, and your opener sequence.

 
Hero Talent Master Switches

 You can use the master switches below to flip the entire page's options to your selected choice.

 Best Beast Mastery Hunter Single Target Rotation

 Beast Mastery Hunter in Single-Target plays around a priority list, juggling both ability cooldowns and resources based on an order of power. This means with each GCD we go top to bottom on a list, and press the button with the current highest value. With selected, the priority is as follows: With selected, the priority is as follows:

 Please select a Hero Talent option to generate a Single Target priority 

 The builds used below are covered in the Talents page. Anywhere you see the icon, you can hover over it for additional notes. 

The rotation for aims to primarily play around Nature's Ally , but is otherwise very straightforward.

 
Priority

 
 Cast Barbed Shot if Bestial Wrath is about to come off cooldown in the next 3 seconds.

 Cast Bestial Wrath . 

 Cast Kill Command if you have a Howl of the Pack Leader buff or Nature's Ally active. 

 Cast Barbed Shot . 

 Cast Cobra Shot . 
 

 The builds used below are covered in the Talents page. Anywhere you see the icon, you can hover over it for additional notes. 

The rotation plays around your cooldown window a bit and weaves between Kill Command s, Barbed Shot s and Black Arrow s.

 
Priority

 
 Cast Bestial Wrath . 

 Cast Kill Command if you have the Nature's Ally buff active. 

 Cast Black Arrow if Withering Fire is active. 

 Cast Wailing Arrow . 

 Cast Barbed Shot . 

 Cast Black Arrow . 

 Cast Cobra Shot . 
 

 Further Details 

 
 The priority changes when Withering Fire fades and Bestial Wrath is still active. During this small period, you should aim to use Barbed Shot over Black Arrow . 

 Wailing Arrow can be used in a variety of spots in your cooldown window, as it is available for 15 seconds. Make sure you do not waste other resources when you use it, such as allowing Kill Command to reach 2 charges. Good RNG with Soul Drinker can delay it for quite a bit but you should make sure you always get it off. 
 

 
 Best Beast Mastery Hunter AoE Rotation

AoE primarily adds Wild Thrash to the mix, which is a powerful instant AoE hit which activates Beast Cleave . With selected, the priority is as follows: With selected, the priority is as follows:

 Please select a Hero Talent option to generate a Single Target priority 

 The builds used below are covered in the Talents page. Anywhere you see the icon, you can hover over it for additional notes. 

Your AoE rotation is very similar to your single-target one, with one additional button. Note that you should NOT aim to multi-dot Barbed Shot .

 
Priority

 
 Cast Barbed Shot at your priority target if Bestial Wrath is about to come off cooldown. 

 Cast Bestial Wrath as long as Beast Cleave is active.

 Cast Wild Thrash 

 Cast Kill Command 

 Cast Barbed Shot at your priority target. 

 Cast Cobra Shot 
 

 Further Details 

On AoE as , it's important to optimize your use Stampede! usage:
 
 You should think about where you are standing relative to the enemy as you go into your cooldown window. You should aim to be at a similar height as the enemy, and not too far away.

If the enemy is about to die, or move, it might be worth delaying your cooldown window.
 

 The builds used below are covered in the Talents page. Anywhere you see the icon, you can hover over it for additional notes. 

Your AoE rotation is very similar to your single-target one, with an additional button added. Note that you should NOT aim to multi-dot Barbed Shot .

 
Priority

 Cast Black Arrow if Withering Fire is up.

 Further Details 

 
 Every Black Arrow you cast will fire a Bleak Powder cone behind its target, applying Black Arrow s damage-over-time effect. This means you generally want to try and aim Black Arrow s at enemies near the front of the pack, to ensure maximum cleave.

Pre-Combat Checks

Before any combat happens, Beast Mastery Hunters should make sure to do the following things. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.

 Beast Mastery Hunter Major Cooldowns

Beast Mastery Hunter has one cooldown in Bestial Wrath , which has a short CD, but is highly impactful. It has a very large amount of effects tied into itself, and both Hero Trees change it in different ways. You will be aiming to play around it as much as possible.

 
 Bestial Wrath 

 
The most important aspect is that you use Bestial Wrath on cooldown, as often as you possibly can. It sounds simple but losing one use loses a lot of damage.

While there are a lot of talents that interact with Bestial Wrath , most of them are passive and not worth playing around. 

 Bloodshed will be applied to the target the pet is currently attacking. If your pet is not attacking anything, you will not get a bleed. 

 Nature's Ally will make your Kill Command more powerful, indirectly, since there is one additional pet casting it. 

The initial hit of Bestial Wrath is fairly large and more importantly, affected by Beast Cleave . When combined with Nature's Ally , this makes every individual additional hit of Bestial Wrath trigger their own Beast Cleave .

 For : 
You will cause your next Kill Command to trigger a Stampede! 

This will fire a line of animals 30 yards in front of you. These animals have no height and will not adjust for curves in the terrain. This means they miss very easily.
 
 For : 
You will gain one Deathblow .

You will gain Withering Fire , making your Black Arrow s more powerful for a short period. 

 Wailing Dead summons one Dark Hound . 
This Hound , will, notably, trigger Pact of the Hollow , making Kill Command notably stronger.

The Dark Hound will do a lot of damage and also benefits from Dire Cleave . This can turn Bestial Wrath into an AoE burst cooldown at the cost of only one talent point.
 
 Wailing Dead also gives you access to Wailing Arrow , which can be used both for its large damage and the AoE silence effect.

As this is your only form of cooldown, you will want to line up Racial Abilities , Trinkets (which buff your stats), and Potions with it. 

 
 Trinkets, Potions and Racials

 
For Trinkets :
Any trinket that increases your stats, including as Light Company Guidon , Void Execution Mandate , Algeth'ar Puzzle Box , Emberwing Feather and Freightrunner's Flask , should be used alongside Bestial Wrath . 
Note that Algeth'ar Puzzle Box has a two second cast time. This means that you want to use it two seconds before the encounter starts, and two seconds before Bestial Wrath is available. 
 

Any trinket that simply does damage, should just be used on cooldown, such as Latch's Crooked Hook , Ranger-Captain's Iridescent Insignia and Void Stalker's Contract . 

For Potions : 
You should use your potion alongside your Bestial Wrath . Note that it needs to be active before the initial hit so that too gets boosted. Macro-ing it to Bestial Wrath works for this. 

You should look to use your potions alongside your trinkets or racials, as long as it does not cost you a usage of your potion. 
 

For Racials : 
Any racial that increases your stats, such as Berserking , Ancestral Call , Fireblood and Blood Fury , should be used alongside Bestial Wrath . 

You should look to use your racial alongside your trinkets or potion, as long as it does not cost you a usage of your racial. 

Any other racial should not be used rotationally, you would rather use a Cobra Shot . 
 

 Beast Mastery Hunter Advanced Tips

Beast Mastery Hunter, while simple, has a few tips and tricks that, while not showing up in the rotation above, do net you notable damage increases overall. These are mostly contained in the below two categories.

 
Perfecting your cooldown window

 
 As you approach your cooldown window, you should start planning towards having two charges of Kill Command available. If you are , make sure you do not have any Deathblow active as Withering Fire will give one for you. 

 Make sure your pet is attacking your current priority target, so that Bloodshed lasts its full duration. If your pet is not attacking anything, you do not get a bleed. 

Check out the UI & Macros page for pet attack macros.
 

 Any item that boosts your direct damage (such as a potion or a trinket that gives any stat but haste) should be active before Bestial Wrath strikes the target, so that it benefits. 
 
Macroing them together is fine for this purpose. 
 

 On AoE, make sure that you have Beast Cleave active when you press Bestial Wrath , so you get a big AoE burst. 
 During the cooldown itself, you should aim to spend as many Kill Command s as possible, and buff them all with Nature's Ally . 
 Since your cooldown is so short, you might get it back towards the end of Mythic+ packs. It might be wise to hold it if you don't anticipate the encounter lasting much longer. 

 For : 
 You should think about where you are standing relative to the enemy as you go into your cooldown window. You should aim to be at a similar height as the enemy, and not too far away.

If the enemy is about to die, or move, it might be worth delaying your cooldown window.

If using Killer Cobra , you should look to prioritize Cobra Shot over Barbed Shot during Bestial Wrath .
 

 For : 
The Dark Hound with Dire Cleave causes your cooldown to gain a powerful AoE burst component. Take advantage of this in raid when not running a full AoE setup, and line it up with important add spawns. 

 Note that the priority changes when Withering Fire fades and Bestial Wrath is still active. During this small period, you should aim to use Barbed Shot over Black Arrow . 

 Wailing Arrow is generally flexible in how you use it but you should generally avoid wasting resources while using it, such as Kill Command reaching two charges. You should, however, always use it before the effect runs out. You also have the option of taking advantage of silence effect in Mythic+.
 

 
 Pet Management 

Pets are notoriously awkward to manage, so this section will cover various tips and tricks to make this task easier and more effective. 

 
For AoE, it's relatively important that your pet(s) are central in the pack to maximize the amount of targets hit by Beast Cleave and Wild Thrash . Pets will generally try to attack the back of the mob, so try to move them to target an enemy whose back is towards the middle of the pack. 

 The UI & Macros page has various tools to help control your pets better, including a solution to their broken autocast and various pet attack macros. 

 Pets like to get stuck a lot! Generally speaking, your best solution to this is either using your pets' "Follow" or "Passive" commands, or swapping between them. Make sure you have these bound to reasonable keys, as each problem may have a different solution. In a worst-case scenario, you will have to dismiss your pet and resummon it. On some encounters, your pet may die from improperly coded AoE, and on others, they may move out of range and despawn.

 Your Kill Command and Barbed Shot will cause your pet charge towards the target. This is important to keep in mind when target-swapping, as you will want to make good use of these effectively to minimize your pets' downtime. 

 Your pet also has Dash , which you can manually use to move it around quickly. It is set to auto-cast by default, which often wastes it. 

 It's worth turning off Spirit Walk auto-cast, as it makes your pet start attacking the enemy slower.
 

Our Beast Mastery Hunter guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on View Changelog in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Beast Mastery Hunter guides for , make sure to browse the Navigation Bar at the top of the page.

This will require you standing still. If Bestial Wrath is about to expire, make sure to still cast this.

When Bestial Wrath is about to come off cooldown you want to try to save so that you have two charges available.

While this is your highest priority, you should NOT open with it, as if your pet is not attacking your target, you will not apply Bloodshed . See the opener section.

Make sure your pet is positioned in the center of the enemy pack so that this and Beast Cleave can strike as many enemies as possible. 

Remember that your pet will always try to melee attack its target from the back.
